title: Why the Tray in Your Microwave Spins
fb_caption: Ever get a hot spoonful and a lukewarm one from the same bowl of soup? Microwaves bounce around inside the oven. Some spots get more energy than others. The turntable carries food through those spots, but the very center of the tray stays put. A stir halfway through can help even out the heat. Which leftover do you always stop to stir?
engagement_comment: Which leftover always gets a halfway stir at your house? Soup, chili, or something else?

beats.text: Why can one spoonful of microwaved soup be piping hot when the next is barely warm?
Microwaves bounce off the metal walls and overlap, so some spots get more energy than others.
Water molecules in your soup absorb that energy. Where they absorb more, the soup can heat up faster.
The glass tray turns to carry different parts of your soup through stronger and weaker spots.
But watch the very center of that spinning tray. It stays in the same spot the whole time.
Stirring halfway through helps even out the heat. Which leftovers do you always stop to stir? Tell us below.
